pathogen_scientific_name.quote: caused by the oomycete (not a true fungus) pathogen Peronospora trifoliorum

type_of_disease.quote: Downy mildew is primarily caused by the oomycete (not a true fungus) pathogen Peronospora trifoliorum

affected_parts.quote: The disease begins as chlorotic spots on the leaflets. ... Infected stems are usually a little larger than non-infected stems ... particularly troublesome on newly germinating seedlings. Infected seedlings are weakened ... Seedling death

summary.value: The disease begins as chlorotic spots on the leaflets that may enlarge to cover the entire leaflet, with leaflets becoming twisted and margins curling down; infected stems are thickened with bunchy, rosette-like growth at their tips, and a white to grayish downy growth appears on the underside of infected leaflets.
summary.quote: The disease begins as chlorotic spots on the leaflets. As the disease progresses, these chlorotic areas may enlarge and eventually cover the entire leaflet. Infected leaflets become twisted and the margins curl down. Infected stems are usually a little larger than non-infected stems and produce bunchy, rosette-like growth at their tips. The tell-tale sign of downy mildew is the production of a white to grayish downy growth on the underside of infected leaflets.

diagnostic_features.value: The tell-tale sign of downy mildew is the production of a white to grayish downy growth on the underside of infected leaflets.
diagnostic_features.quote: The tell-tale sign of downy mildew is the production of a white to grayish downy growth on the underside of infected leaflets.

value: Plant resistant/tolerant alfalfa cultivars (resistant varieties available for P. trifoliorum)
Fungicide seed treatments with metalaxyl or mefenoxam to manage seedling infection
Do not delay the first spring cutting; harvest early to remove inoculum and susceptible tissue and reduce losses
Cutting reduces humidity in the canopy, lowering infection risk
Spring seeding is recommended where fall infections are common
treatments.quote: Resistant alfalfa cultivars are available to economically manage downy mildew. Fungicide seed treatments such as metalaxyl and mefenoxam effectively manage seedling downy mildew. When downy mildew is severe, do not delay the first harvest.

conflicts.note: NMSU describes downy mildew as a 'fungal disease', but Crop Protection Network and USU Extension correctly classify the pathogen as an oomycete (Oomycota), more closely related to algae than true fungi. Canonical value reflects current taxonomy (2 sources agree on Oomycete).

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: The most important causal pathogen is S. botryosum , which has two distinct biotypes that cause disease within differing temperature regimes.

summary.value: The disease produces leaf lesions whose appearance depends on the biotype: W-T causes brown, oval lesions with dark margins and yellow halos that may develop concentric rings, while C-T causes small, irregular, light-colored lesions with dark margins.

summary.value: The most obvious symptom is premature defoliation from the base of the stem upward, with leaf spots appearing first; leaf spots begin as brown areas with a wavy margin, turning gray or silvery as spores are produced, often surrounded by a diffuse yellow margin, and brown lesions also form on stems.
summary.quote: Defoliation from the base of the stem to the top is the most obvious symptom, but leaf spots usually appear first. Leaf spots begin as brown areas with a wavy margin. diagnostic_features.value: Ash-gray, roughly circular leaf spots surrounded by a diffuse yellow margin, which are quite distinct and can be distinguished from other leaf spot diseases once familiar.
diagnostic_features.quote: the leaf spots ... become ash-gray, roughly circular, and surrounded by a diffuse yellow margin (Figure 3) . These spots are quite distinct and once familiar with them, can easily be distinguished from those of other leaf spot diseases.

value: Avoid planting particularly susceptible alfalfa cultivars.
Harvest early, when flower buds first appear / before extensive defoliation occurs, to minimize losses.
Scout fields regularly during the growing season for early detection of disease so that timely adjustment of cutting schedules can be made.
Adjusting the cutting schedule to disease development is the most practical and economical means of management in established stands.
